title: Dependency and Supply-Chain Security knowledge check

questions.prompt: What should happen at an external trust boundary?
options: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
Cast it to the desired interface and skip validation.
Trust client-submitted roles and ownership fields.
Return secrets in logs to simplify debugging.
questions.answer_key: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
questions.explanation: Compile-time types do not validate external values or enforce authorization by themselves.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Dependency and Supply-Chain Security”?
options: The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with dependency auditing and checked against its intended contract.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with dependency auditing and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Dependency auditing”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Dependency and Supply-Chain Security”?
options: Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check lockfiles and updates, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume evaluating package trust and maintenance is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
questions.answer_key: Check lockfiles and updates, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Lockfiles and updates”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
